ucse.book.pageintro: Hello and welcome to Unique Crops! Here in this book, you'll find information on the various different crops, and how to grow them. A general rule to remember here is that not all the crops will be grown the same way, so be sure to read up on some of them! Luck favors the prepared, or so they say, heheh. Additionally, what they drop may have various amounts of usefulness. It is completely up to you to find out what's good or not.
ucse.book.pagenormal: Normalish crops. They can be grown like any other vanilla crops. Aside from being one of the ingredients used to craft this book, there is nothing special about them. Randomly drops vanilla crops when harvested.
ucse.book.pagecinderbella: Based on the old folktale, these crops are quite magical: they must be planted between sunset and midnight while surrounded on all 4 sides by pumpkins. If it is not planted and harvested in this fashion, it withers away.
ucse.book.pagecollis: These crops likes being planted in high places, usually on mountains. Also, the higher up they're planted, the faster they can grow when receiving growth ticks.
ucse.book.pagedirigible: These dirigible plums seems to be filled with helium, that would explain why some fully grown plums keep flying away! Best to pick up the plums when they drop as soon as possible.
ucse.book.pageenderlily: These ender lilies just love to have nearby empty farmland to teleport to. Sometimes they'll even swap places with other kinds of crops. Not crops of the same type as them, though... Once mature, you can harvest them for twine or throw an Ender Pearl at them to painfully create more pearls.
ucse.book.pageferoxia: Much like breaking in wild horses, these savage plants all have different ways of being grown. Once planted or harvested manually, this book will keep a record of their current demands for each stage of crop growth on the next page. These crops seem to be locked to the players who planted them, so one may have to be ingame in order for them to grow. Additionally, the steps will be different once a fully grown crop is harvested.
ucse.book.pageinvisibilia: Once planted, these sneaky crops will be completely invisible to anyone that doesn't happen to be wearing a certain kind of eyewear. They can be harvested normally once you can see them.
ucse.book.pageknowledge: Their thirst for knowledge knows no bounds, these crops will search for nearby bookshelves in a small radius, then look into any inventory above the bookshelves for written books to read. If they find one, they'll grow by one stage for every page. It's good to note that they don't seem to like book copies, and each book can only be read once.
ucse.book.pagemaryjane: Blazing plants! These prefer the hellish environment of the Nether. Once fully grown, these crops will only be successfully harvested when the harvester is on fire, else the plants themselves burst into flames. Though they don't respond to bone meal, Blaze Powder can be used instead for the same effect.
ucse.book.pagemerlinia: Like the classic book written by T.H. White, this crop appears to move backwards through time, starting at appearing fully planted, and working backwards to the youngest stage. This only happens when they're given a special kind of bone meal.
ucse.book.pagemillennium: This crop takes a very long time to grow. I'm not even sure what they'll drop. Growth accelerators from other mods are a must.
ucse.book.pagemusica: These crops will grow by dancing to the beat: Note Block drums, specifically. What kind of songs they'll like is completely up to you. Drops a random music disc.
ucse.book.pageprecision: These bright sparkers are quite precise! So precise, that there is only a small window where they can be harvested for anything useful. Take cues from their appearance, or check for a redstone signal.
ucse.book.pageweepingbells: They're quite shy, but also in need of your attentions. Weeping Bells will only grow when you're looking directly at them. Once fully grown, do not take your eyes off of them, lest you face their wrath from your attentions being divided elsewhere.
ucse.book.pageeula: They are possibly the most legal crops you can get. Of course, once you get past all the legal mumbo jumbo when planting them, that is.
ucse.book.pagedyeius: Dye plants! Instead of planting and harvesting different plants for each dye, everything is condensed into one crop. Its appearance and drops depend on the time of day or night.
ucse.book.pagecobblonia: Hardy plants! They may look a little rocky, but they can prove to be quite useful in some circumstances. Once fully grown, you may have water on one side of the soil it is on and lava on the opposite side for free cobble being given out at random.
ucse.book.pageabstract: I must admit, I cheated a little in order to snag a picture of one actually planted. These crops, being just an abstract concept, will not materialize into the world as a form of "crops", instead implanting the idea of growth in their planter and gradually producing their output directly into your inventory.
ucse.book.pageartisia: These plants are pretty crafty! They're the next step you need to get to in order to craft the other seeds. You'll need 9 of them in a 3x3 square, with the center one being grown last. After that, it is just a matter of dropping the desired ingredients on top of the center plant, upon which it will automatically try crafting the output once all 9 plants have the ingredients. The order you put the ingredients in doesn't matter. Rightclick a crop to retrieve the item it's holding.
ucse.book.pagewafflonia: These crops only grow when together with other crops of their type, in any square or rectangle shape that's at least 2x2. Harvesting them will yield waffles, part of a delicious breakfast diet.
ucse.book.pagedevilsnare: Thorny plants that grow well in darkness, they will shrink away if exposed to too much sky. Additionally, they will try to spread to adjacent dirt/farmland once fully grown. Fully matured crops will snare and slow down any players that walk through them.
ucse.book.pagepixelsius: Pixelly, pixelly pixel plants. Starting from the default 16x16 textures, these crops will gradually get more and more high definition as they grow.
ucse.book.pagepetramia: Very bedrocky crops, these can only be planted within 10 blocks of the dimension floor. Once fully grown, they gradually transform all bedrock around and below them into Dark Blocks, which can be picked up by sneak-rightclicking with an Ender Snooker. If mobGriefing gamemode is off, then the crops will instead yield the Dark Blocks when rightclicked. Dark Blocks have potential use for recipes, and are also very good Witherproof blocks.
ucse.book.pagemalleatoris: Crafted using anvils as part of the seed recipe, these are the renewable versions of anvils. To grow, they must have items with durability nearby. The higher the durability of these items, the better the chance they'll advance a stage. This process will consume 10%% of that item's durability. Once fully grown, right clicking it with any repairable item will restore 50%% of that item's max durability.
ucse.book.pageimperia: These imperius crops are known for their strong anti mob spawning policies. Growing them up requires killing the random mobs they spawn, though. Once fully grown, they will prevent mobs from spawning in a 3x3 chunk area around them.
ucse.book.pagelacusia: Lacusia crops will transport items from A to B, only along a flat surface. When a crop next to an inventory is given a redstone signal, it will extract any items from that inventory, then transport them along until it finds an available inventory to insert into. When it reaches a junction, it will loop through the directions (S-W-N-E) for the first valid crop/inventory to insert into. If the junction is given a redstone signal, it will reverse the direction to search in.
ucse.book.pagehexis: Experience crops will not grow unless given experience orbs or by right-clicking them to feed them your XP levels. Once grown, glass bottles can be used to collect the experience with a right-click. There is a 50/50 chance this will reset the crop's growth.
ucse.book.pageindustria: Their photosynthetic process allows them to store up the sun's energy as actual stored energy. A harvest of a fully grown crop will yield beans more powerful than potatoes.
ucse.book.pagequarry: This crop is so hardy, it hardly grows at all! One must mine this hard plant with a vanilla pickaxe to grow it. Once mature, it mines up every block in its chunk below itself (ignoring farmland, crops, unbreakable blocks and blocks with internal data, like chests). It preserves blocks perfectly and puts them into any chest above itself (or moves blocks to that spot if the space is empty). The Fossura requires wheat to be planted around it, so it can steal their growth to power its mining.
ucse.book.pagedonutsteel: An original crop, licensed and copyrighted by EULA crop. Original content, donut steel. Will pop out of the ground and try to kill you if you harvest it. A method by which all damage it deals you can be redirected may exist, somewhere.
ucse.book.pageinstabilis: These metastable crops exist in a state where delicate harvesting is needed to handle them. Bring shears, lest you yield nothing when the whole crops break. They need to be surrounded by each other in order to grow.
ucse.book.pagesucco: These vampiric crops suck, but that doesn't mean they are useless. Once planted, they will only grow during the full moon, when their incorporeal form turns corporeal. They turn ghostly at other phases of the moon and invisible during the new moon.
ucse.book.pagemagnes: Crops with a magnetic personality. In fact, they are so magnetic, they can attract one another. Growing two crops of opposing polarities more than one block apart will make them move towards each other. The farther apart they are, the more likely they will drop their item. One can use blue or red dye to change their polarity.
ucse.blank_feroxia_steps: Plant your first Feroxia Seed to set these.
ucse.book.page.book_discount: Harvested from Scientia crops.$(br2)Combine it in an anvil with an enchantable item. That item will thereafter cost 5 levels less to combine with Enchanted Books, though never less than 1.
ucse.book.page.cinderleaf: Harvested from Mary Jane crops.$(br2)Drop 4 of them into source water to convert it into lava.
ucse.book.page.timemeal: Use this on Merlinia plants to make them grow backward until they're fully-grown again. It's the only way to get any output from those crops.
ucse.book.page.potionreverse: Inverts most potion effects currently on the drinker. Blindness becomes Night Vision and vice versa, Poison swaps with Regeneration, and so on.
ucse.book.page.potionzombification: Turns the drinker into a Zombie Villager when the effect expires. Cannot be removed with Milk. (Make sure your will is up to date.)
ucse.book.page.potionennui: Puts the drinker into a state of crushing apathy where they cannot jump, break blocks, or interact with things. What would be the point? Life is a black pit of despair.
ucse.book.page.potionignorance: Prevents mobs from noticing the drinker.
ucse.book.page.slippers: A single Glass Slipper is harvested from Cinderbella crops. It can't be worn, but if it's in your inventory when you kill a mob that's wearing boots, you might find the other slipper and form a pair, which is wearable and makes you immune to Devil's Snares and to damage from standing on Cactus.
ucse.book.page.weepingeye: Throw this to illuminate all mobs near the impact spot for several seconds.
ucse.book.page.book_upgrade1: Use an anvil to combine one of the following items with an Upgrade Book to improve it by +1. Reaching +10 often gives it a bonus effect.
ucse.book.page.book_upgrade2: $(li)Precision Axe$(li)Precision Pickaxe$(li)Precision Sword$(li)Precision Shovel$(li)Comfy Poncho$(li)3D Glasses$(li)Pixel Glasses$(li)Item Magnet$(li)Seven-League Boots
ucse.book.page.eggupgrade: Use this on a chicken to make it lay eggs faster. Killing the chicken gives you the upgrade back.
ucse.book.page.easybadge: Keep this in your inventory to make some nearby mobs less dangerous:$(li)Creepers take longer to explode.$(li)Skeletons shoot less often.$(li)Zombies don't summon reinforcements.
ucse.book.page.book_eula: Throw this burdensome book via rightclick. If it hits a player (including YOU) they'll be forced to click through several pages of legal agreements. Quite annoying (and legally unenforceable).
ucse.book.page.escaperope: This single-use item teleports you straight up to the highest possible block you can stand on.
ucse.book.page.ferromagnetic_iron: Occasionally produced when two Magnes crops collide.
ucse.book.page.spirit_bait: Use this bait on a Harvest Trap to make it more likely to sparkle.
ucse.book.page.golden_bread: As nutritious as bread, with the added bonus of several minutes of Luck II.
ucse.book.page.diet_pills: These pills make you hungrier instead of fuller.
ucse.book.page.large_plum: Consuming one will give you the Levitation effect for two seconds, or enough time to consume the next Large Plum to continue levitating higher until you run out of food and plummet to your death.
ucse.book.page.precision_axe: Comes pre-enchanted with Silk Touch.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to give it a chance of chopping heads off Creepers, Zombies, Skeletons and Wither Skeletons.
ucse.book.page.precision_pick: Comes pre-enchanted with Silk Touch.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to allow it to collect spawners and infested blocks.
ucse.book.page.precision_shovel: Comes pre-enchanted with Silk Touch.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to prevent nearby sand and gravel from falling while you're holding it.
ucse.book.page.precision_sword: Comes pre-enchanted with Looting I.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to ignore the normal 1/2 second damage immunity.
ucse.book.page.precision_hammer: Comes pre-enchanted with Silk Touch. Counts as the correct tool for mining all blocks.
ucse.book.page.glasses_3d: Necessary to see Invisibilia crops and Glass.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to automatically gain Night Vision in low light.
ucse.book.page.poncho: The wearer of this chest armor falls at a slow, safe speed.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 to make most mobs ignore you.
ucse.book.page.glasses_pixels: Provides you with a toggleable low-res pixel-vision mode.$(br2)Upgrade to +10 and you can sometimes find special blocks deep underground...
ucse.book.page.cactus_armor: Each piece of this armor set comes pre-enchanted with Thorns II.
ucse.book.page.endersnooker: Use this on a mob to swap places with it, or sneak-rightclick on an unbreakable Dark Block to pick it up.
ucse.book.page.handmirror: If held in your off-hand, the Hand Mirror automatically reflects Guardian lasers so they damage themselves instead of you.
ucse.book.page.batstaff: Instantly kills all bats near you, without loot or XP.
ucse.book.page.phantomstaff: Instantly kills all phantoms near you, without loot or XP.
ucse.book.page.thunderpantz: Sneak and walk on carpet to build up a static charge. Once charged, Thunder Pants deal lightning damage to the first thing that hits you in melee.
ucse.book.page.bean_battery: Harvested from Industria crops. Intended for use with other mods where a pre-charged personal FE battery item might come in handy.
ucse.book.page.demo_cord: Harvested from Instabilis crops. Can be placed on the ground like Redstone Dust, then detonated with a redstone signal. Much more controlled than TNT.
ucse.book.page.steel_donut: Dropped by the Battle Crop that spawns from picking Donut Steel -- if you kill it properly.
ucse.book.page.wildwood_staff: The Wildwood Staff is required to form most Supercrop multiblocks. Charge the Staff with Crop Power by holding it in your main hand while crops grow around you.$(br2)Hold an Orb of Good Harvest in your off-hand to collect Crop Power from a larger area and charge the Staff faster.
ucse.book.page.vampiric_ointment: Harvested from Succo crops. Use the Ointment on a non-boss mob to link yourself to it, then place the Ointment in a Golden Goblet. Any damage you would suffer will be dealt to the mob instead.
ucse.book.page.ankh: A Flint Ankh in your inventory prevents you from dropping it or the 8 items around it when you die. This costs its durability.
ucse.book.page.impact_shield: After it blocks enough hits, the Impact Shield sets off a large mob-damaging explosion. The explosion won't hurt you or break blocks. You won't be able to block with the shield again for several seconds.
ucse.book.page.brass_knuckles: A rare weapon, generally only found as chest loot. It deals melee damage and knockback after a brief delay.
ucse.book.page.pixel_brush: Used with the Weatherflesia supercrop to paint biomes.
ucse.book.page.rubiks_cube1: Stores up to 6 teleport locations, one per color face. Sneak-rightclick the Cube on a block to save that location for the current face. Change faces by rightclicking the Cube in the air and using the WASD keys. Teleport to a stored location by rotating to its face and clicking the menu button.
ucse.book.page.rubiks_cube2: (Note: The Cube only rotates in the GUI, not your hand.)
ucse.book.page.item_magnet: Picks up nearby items. Can be toggled on and off. Upgrading it increases its range.
ucse.book.page.seven_league_boots: Increases the wearer's step height and jump height, and gives a speed boost while sprinting. Upgrading it makes the boost even faster.
ucse.book.page.enchanted_leather: First, craft Impregnated Leather. Then hold it in your main hand and stand near growing crops until it collects enough Crop Power.
ucse.book.page.oldbow: A bow that shoots as in ages past. Attaining one requires turning back the Hourglass -- they don't make 'em like this anymore.
ucse.book.page.dyedbonemeal: Dyed variants of regular bone meal. Depending on the color, they may create specific flowers or other plants if used on grass blocks. They behave as ordinary bone meal otherwise.
ucse.book.page.emblem_melee: Slightly reduces the wait time between swings of a tool or weapon, or when switching between them.
ucse.book.page.emblem_scarab: Nullifies all potion effects on you. Even good ones.
ucse.book.page.emblem_transformation: Has a small chance of polymorphing any non-boss mob you hit into another one.
ucse.book.page.emblem_powerfist: If you are empty-handed, you break stone-type blocks quickly, even if you're off the ground or underwater. But the blocks are destroyed.
ucse.book.page.emblem_rainbow: Sheep you shear give random-colored wool.
ucse.book.page.emblem_food: Automatically feeds you, at the cost of its durability.
ucse.book.page.emblem_ironstomach: You can eat nuggets, ingots and gems. Some valuable ones also grant potion effects.
ucse.book.page.emblem_defense: Automatically blocks all arrows for you simply by having a shield in your off-hand.
ucse.book.page.emblem_leaf: Provides additional Toughness for each piece of your armor above leather tier.
ucse.book.page.emblem_pacifism: All direct damage you suffer is reduced to 0.$(br)All direct damage you deal is also reduced to 0.
ucse.book.page.emblem_blacksmith: Anvils won't degrade when you use them.
ucse.book.page.emblem_weight: You toss items much farther. Some can deal damage.
ucse.book.page.emblem_bookworm: You can eat Enchanted Books. Rare and higher-level enchantments are more filling.
ucse.book.page.hourglass: Toss this on the ground (it won't despawn), or build it and power it with redstone, to slowly transform certain nearby blocks into older-looking versions: Grass, Gravel, Cobblestone, Mossy Cobblestone, Brick blocks, and blocks of Iron, Gold and Diamond.
ucse.book.page.totemhead: Makes nearby mobs invisible. (Surely you have a reason for doing this.)
ucse.book.page.dreamcatcher: When built directly over the head of a bed, players with that bed as their spawn point will not attract Phantoms.
ucse.book.page.lavalily: Placed on lava instead of water. Sets mobs and players on fire, though players can avoid this by wearing boots.
ucse.book.page.icelily: Placed on water or any ice or snow block. Items that fall on them never despawn.
ucse.book.page.junglelily: Placed on water like normal. Negates fall damage.
ucse.book.page.enderlily: Placed on water like normal. If built directly above each other within 12 blocks, players can jump or crouch on one to teleport up or down to the next.
ucse.book.page.darkblock: Unbreakable, Wither-proof Dark Blocks are created by growing a Petramia crop near Bedrock. Can only be collected by sneak-rightclicking with an Ender Snooker. This will leave Bedrock behind if the Dark Block was in the lowest two levels of the dimension.
ucse.book.page.sun_dial: Emits a redstone signal every day, around the time the Sundial was built. Or rightclick it to change that to the current time. Perfect for Dyeius crops.
ucse.book.page.abstractbarrel: This barrel holds 100 slots of items, but the GUI only shows you 4 of those slots. At random. And they change every time you open it.$(br2)Breaking it DELETES everything inside.
ucse.book.page.invisibilia_glass: Players can only see Invisibilia Glass if they're wearing 3D Glasses. But if you can't see it, you can walk right through it, because OBVIOUSLY nothing is there.$(br2)Will always block mobs and items.
ucse.book.page.sun_block: The Sun Block of Fertility allows a few select Unique Crops to ignore their special requirements and grow like normal. It must be next to the crop and powered with redstone.
ucse.book.page.harvest_trap: This totem sporadically traps a hypothetical spirit to boost the growth of nearby plants. Occasionally it will attract a particularly powerful spirit and sparkle. Rightclick it before the sparkles fade for a surge of serious growth.
ucse.book.page.bucketrope: Rightclick this with an empty bucket to retrieve whatever fluid lies directly below. Distance doesn't matter as long as nothing is in the way.
ucse.book.page.cindertorch: This is no torch, but a lantern. It can be waterlogged or placed on walls.
ucse.book.page.obtuse_platform: The Obtuse Platform looks solid, but it isn't. Falling through it from any height sets your fall distance to 20 blocks.
ucse.tooltip.discountbook: Craft with any tool or armor. Makes subsequent repairs cheaper.
ucse.tooltip.eggupgrade: Stuff this in a chicken to make it lay eggs faster.
ucse.tooltip.upgradebook: Combine with tools and armor that can be upgraded in an anvil.
ucse.tooltip.slipperglass: Go hunt for mobs wearing boots with this in your inventory.
ucse.tooltip.easybadge: Keep in hotbar. Makes some mobs easier to deal with.
ucse.tooltip.eulabook: Players being disruptive in court? Throw the book at them!
ucse.tooltip.escaperope: Consumable item: Sends the player to the highest block directly above them. Works in the nether.
ucse.tooltip.sundial: Emits redstone signal based on the time of day you set it at.
ucse.tooltip.batstaff: GET RID OF THOSE PESKY BATS. NO DROPS.
ucse.tooltip.phantomstaff: GET RID OF THOSE PESKY PHANTOMS. NO DROPS.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_defense: Blocks arrow damage so long as you have a shield equipped in the off hand.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_food: Automatically fills up your hunger at the cost of emblem's durability.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_ironstomach: Grants an appetite for certain metals and gems.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_leaf: Gain additional toughness for each piece of armor above leather tier.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_melee: Reduces recharge time on attack strength.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_powerfist: Enables faster block mining as long as the main hand has no items equipped.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_rainbow: Allows shearing sheep for wool of a random color.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_scarab: Nullifies all potion effects, good or bad.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_transformation: Has a chance of transforming a mob when hitting them.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_pacifism: Reduces all damage you give and take to 0.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_blacksmith: Any work done on an anvil will not damage the anvil.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_weight: Any thrown items will have farther distance. Some will hurt.
ucse.tooltip.emblem_bookworm: Makes enchanted books edible. The more enchantments on one, the more filling.
ucse.tooltip.ointment.empty: Rightclick on any non-player, non-boss creature.
ucse.tooltip.ointment.filled: Put in a goblet placed on the ground.
ucse.tooltip.thunderpantz: Sneak around on carpet to build up static electricity!
ucse.tooltip.rubikscube: Rightclick to open GUI. Crouch + rightclick to set teleport.
ucse.tooltip.impact_shield: Absorbs damage while blocking with it. Explodes on last durability, followed by a cooldown.
ucse.tooltip.sun_block: When powered, allows certain crops directly adjacent to it to ignore their own growth conditions.
ucse.tooltip.bootsleague: Boots that are speedy. Sprinting will give a brief burst of speed. Strength depends on upgrade level.
ucse.tooltip.item_magnet: Pulls in nearby items. The higher the upgrade level, the bigger the range.
ucse.tooltip.precisionhammer: When all you have is a hammer...
advancement.ucse:craftingMillennium: Some things can take a while
advancement.ucse:craftingMusica: Two to the one to the three
advancement.ucse:craftingLacusia: From point A to point B
advancement.ucse.craftingBlessed.desc: Obtain holy seeds from a priest
advancement.ucse:craftingWildwoodStaff.d: Craft or obtain a Wildwood Staff for the first time.
ucse.condition.hastorch: Player must be holding a torch.
ucse.condition.hellworld: Must be grown in the Nether.
ucse.condition.hungryplant: Leave some food on top of it.
ucse.condition.thirstyplant: Leave a water bucket on top of it.
ucse.condition.fullbrightness: Likes a lot of nearby light.
ucse.condition.likescooking: Needs a nearby furnace smelting stuff.
ucse.condition.likesbrewing: Likes nearby brewing stands brewing stuff.
ucse.enchanting.nothing: You have nothing to enchant in either hand.
ucse.enchanting.missingcrops: Not all hexis crops are present.
ucse.enchanting.cropgrowth: All hexis crops must be at least age %s.

ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.intro: To get started with multiblocks, which is the act of transforming a set of blocks placed into the world into another set of blocks, you need a catalyst. The usual catalyst will be the wildwood staff, along with whatever power is stored in it that the recipes will ask for. Arrange the set of blocks in the world as shown by the recipe input grid, and rightclick the center of the arrangement with the catalyst. If the catalyst is not a wildwood staff, then it is a consumable item.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.craftystalks: Plant all of the Artisia crops as arranged in the recipe window. You do NOT need to fully grow any of them. Once the multiblock is formed, give it some time to grow a crafting table. This part will then provide you with the GUI version of crafting your unique seeds. Placing a wildwood staff in the appropriate slot will let the recipe eat up crop power instead of the crafting ingredients instead.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.cocito: The solution to furnaces only cooking a single item at a time, this crop will smelt multiple dropped items at once. After the items are smelted, if they are left alone, the supercrop will smelt them into useless lumps, so pick them up beforehand.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.exedo: A supercrop that hungers for any nearby living creatures. Once one unlucky victim gets within range, they will shake, and then pounce upon them with large jaws from the earth, swallowing them whole and leaving behind some drops.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.fascino: An enchanting supercrop, the formation of enchantment magic will depend on the formation of the Hexis crops around it. To figure out if the formation is correct, input the ingredients as shown in JEI recipe (right click Enchantment Table block), then grab an enchantable item in the offhand and rightclick the enchanter with a Wildwood staff. Smoke will appear in places where a Hexis crop is needed.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.itero: A supercrop that, when rightclicked, displays a random sequence on pressure plates surrounding it. Follow the sequence correctly to grow the Itero by one stage. Make a mistake and it regresses. You can display the sequence as often as you wish before trying it. Rightclick it when fully grown to harvest ingredients for a Rubik's Cube. NOTE: The Visualizer does not recognize Redstone Dust lines correctly. The Itero will still form.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.portal: Making this portal to the next world will require bricks you will have to find underground in the overworld.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.weatherflesia: A rafflesia-like supercrop that holds information about the biome it's planted in. Rightclicking the center with a Pixelsius Brush will collect that information into it. (Sneak-rightclick to retrieve the brush.) How much information per random tick will depend on how long the plant has stayed since it was formed.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.lignator: A kind of early-game solution to automatically cutting down trees. Create one in the center of a tree farm, and they will periodically grow a block higher, as high as the highest tree block it can find, cutting it down and any nearby logs. When it cannot find any more, the growth is reset. Caution should be taken in cultivating more than one Lignator, as they can chop down other Lignators.
ucse.bookmultiblocks.page.sanalight: This plant brings more than just its own light to bear - it will light up any dark areas in a radius around it with a magical light source. This plant may be broken to remove these light sources, or place alternative sources of light and break the lights by hand.
info.jei.ucse.harvesttrap: Randomly ticks crops in an area around and on the same Y level as it is. Occasionally there is a chance that yellow sparks will emit from the block. Rightclicking it will provide crops around it a speed boost for a short time. Cannot be placed near other harvest traps.
info.jei.ucse.emeradicdiamond: When held in the offhand, along with the Wildwood Staff in the main hand, the orb boosts the range in which to search for nearby vanilla crops to steal growth ticks from.
info.jei.ucse.wildwoodstaff: This staff uses the power of crops to construct multiblocks, enchant, and so on. To fill it up with crop power, one must have vanilla crops growing nearby, in order to steal their growth ticks.
info.jei.ucse.pixelbrush: Setting this inside the center of a Weatherflesia will set its biome to that the Weatherflesia is constructed in. Additionally, the Weatherflesia will charge up the brush, the strength of the charge depending on the length of time from when it was constructed.
info.jei.ucse.precisionaxe: +10 Upgrade: Axe gives beheading abilities to the player who wields it against mobs.
info.jei.ucse.precisionsword: +10 Upgrade: Sword will now ignore the invulnerability time of the victims.
info.jei.ucse.precisionshovel: +10 Upgrade: Breaking sand and gravel will not cause the blocks to fall.
info.jei.ucse.precisionpick: +10 Upgrade: Grants the pickaxe the ability to pick up mob spawners and silverfish blocks.
info.jei.ucse.glasses_3d: +10 Upgrade: Grants night vision to the wearer when in darkness.
info.jei.ucse.poncho: +10 Upgrade: Will make most mobs ignore the wearer.
info.jei.ucse.thunderpantz: Charge speed scales up with upgrade level.
info.jei.ucse.glasses_pixels: +10 Upgrade: Will let the player see unusually pink blocks deep underground when using pixel vision.
info.jei.ucse.flintankh: The Flint Ankh will save any items adjacent to it in the inventory in a 3x3 grid pattern, with the Ankh as the center. It will take damage each time the player dies with it in their inventory.
commands.ucse.error.not_upgradeable: Held item either empty or not upgradeable.
